payload.text:
I want to build a conversational voice-enabled mobile application for civil engineering students and professionals that uses AI vision and voice interaction to identify and explain civil engineering structures, components, and construction elements in real-time.

PROJECT OVERVIEW
App Name: CivilVision AI (or suggest a better name)
Core Functionality:
Users point their phone camera at any civil engineering structure (buildings, bridges, construction sites, structural components), and the app:

Identifies what they're looking at (columns, beams, foundations, walls, etc.)
Analyzes the structural elements visible
Explains via voice conversation the engineering details, specifications, and construction methods
Answers follow-up questions through natural voice dialogue

Target Users:

Civil engineering students (learning on-site during internships/field visits)
Junior engineers on construction sites
Architecture students studying structural systems
Construction supervisors verifying work


PART 1: CORE FEATURES
1. Camera-Based Structure Recognition
Visual Identification Capabilities:
Must accurately identify and explain:
Structural Elements:

Columns: Type (RCC, steel, composite), shape (circular, rectangular, I-beam), reinforcement visible, column-beam connection details
Beams: Type (simply supported, continuous, cantilever), cross-section, stirrup spacing, flexural reinforcement
Slabs: Type (one-way, two-way, flat, waffle), thickness estimation, reinforcement pattern
Foundations: Type (isolated footing, combined, raft, pile cap), depth indicators, soil interface
Walls: Load-bearing vs partition, material (brick, concrete, AAC block), thickness, reinforcement (if RCC)
Staircases: Type (dog-legged, spiral, cantilever), waist slab, tread-riser dimensions
Retaining Walls: Type (gravity, cantilever, counterfort), drainage provisions
Roof Structures: Type (flat, pitched, shell, truss), roofing material, support system

Construction Materials:

Concrete (grade estimation from visual cues)
Steel reinforcement (bar diameter, spacing)
Bricks (type, bonding pattern)
Masonry blocks
Structural steel (sections, connections)
Formwork and falsework

Construction Activities:

Excavation and earthwork
Formwork installation
Reinforcement tying
Concrete pouring
Curing methods
Scaffolding systems

Infrastructure Elements:

Bridges (beam, arch, suspension, cable-stayed)
Tunnels (TBM construction, NATM)
Dams (gravity, arch, buttress)
Roads (pavement layers, drainage)
Metro/railway structures

2. Conversational Voice Interface
Voice Interaction Flow:
Step 1 - Initial Recognition:
User: [Points camera at building with exposed columns]
App: "I can see reinforced concrete columns in this structure. They appear to be rectangular columns, approximately 300mm x 450mm. Would you like me to explain the structural system, the reinforcement details, or the construction method?"
Step 2 - User Query (Voice):
User: "Tell me about the foundation for these columns"
App: "Based on the column size and what appears to be a multi-story structure, these columns likely rest on isolated pad footings. For 300x450mm columns in a building of this scale, typical footing dimensions would be 2m x 2m with a depth of 1.5-2m, depending on soil bearing capacity. The footing would contain a reinforcement mesh of 12mm bars at 150mm spacing both ways. Would you like to know more about the soil investigation process or the design calculations?"
Step 3 - Follow-up Conversation:
User: "What kind of reinforcement is in the columns?"
App: "From the visible construction, these appear to be RCC columns with primary longitudinal reinforcement of 8-12 bars of 16-20mm diameter, arranged around the perimeter. Lateral ties would be 8-10mm diameter bars at 150-200mm spacing to prevent buckling. The actual design would depend on the loads, but this is typical for a column of this size in a 5-6 story building. Should I explain the design code requirements or the construction process?"
Conversation Capabilities:

Answer follow-up questions naturally
Remember context from earlier in the conversation
Ask clarifying questions if image is unclear
Provide different levels of detail (basic vs advanced)
Switch between topics smoothly
Handle interruptions and topic changes

Voice Features:

Hands-free operation (critical for on-site use)
Wake word or push-to-talk button
Natural language understanding (handle casual questions)
Multiple languages (English, Hindi, regional languages)
Adjustable speech speed
Background noise filtering (for construction site environments)

3. Detailed Analysis & Explanation System
For Each Identified Element, Provide:
A. Structural Analysis:

Purpose and function in the structural system
Load transfer mechanism
Critical design considerations
Typical failure modes and prevention
IS Code references (IS 456, IS 800, IS 1893, etc.)

B. Material Specifications:

Concrete grade (M20, M25, M30, etc.)
Steel grade (Fe 415, Fe 500)
Material properties and standards
Quality control requirements
Mix design basics

C. Reinforcement Details:

Main reinforcement (size, spacing, quantity)
Secondary/distribution reinforcement
Minimum and maximum reinforcement ratios
Cover requirements
Splice and anchorage lengths

D. Construction Method:

Step-by-step construction sequence
Formwork requirements
Equipment needed
Labor requirements
Time estimates
Common mistakes to avoid

E. Quality Checks:

What to inspect during construction
Testing requirements (concrete cube test, slump test, etc.)
Acceptance criteria
Common defects and remedies

F. Estimation & Costing:

Material quantities (cement, sand, aggregate, steel)
Approximate cost per unit
Labor costs
Construction duration

G. Design Standards:

Relevant IS codes
Design formulas and principles
Safety factors
Loading considerations

4. Educational Context Features
Learning Modes:
Student Mode:

Simplified explanations with analogies
Step-by-step learning progression
Related topics suggestions
Quiz questions to test understanding
Glossary of terms

Professional Mode:

Technical specifications and calculations
Code compliance checks
Design optimization suggestions
Cost estimation details

Internship Mode:

What to observe on site
Questions to ask site engineers
Safety precautions
Documentation tips

Interactive Learning:

"Show me more examples like this"
"Compare this to [another structure type]"
"What would happen if [scenario]?"
"How is this different from [alternative design]?"

5. AR Overlay & Annotations (Optional Enhancement)
Augmented Reality Features:

Overlay labels on structural elements in real-time
Show hidden reinforcement (X-ray vision mode)
Display dimensions and spacing
Highlight critical zones (high stress areas)
Show construction sequence animation
Compare as-built vs design drawings

6. Reference Library & History
Saved Analysis:

Save photos with AI annotations
Create project folders
Add personal notes and observations
Build a personal reference library

Offline Access:

Download common structure types for offline analysis
Offline voice recognition (limited)
Cached reference materials

Learning History:

Track topics explored
Personalized learning recommendations
Progress tracking for students


PART 2: TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE
Platform & Technology Stack
Mobile App Framework:
Option 1 - Native (Recommended for best performance):

iOS: Swift + SwiftUI
Android: Kotlin + Jetpack Compose
Better camera integration and AR capabilities
Superior voice recognition performance

Option 2 - Cross-Platform (Faster development):

React Native or Flutter
Single codebase for iOS and Android
Good camera and voice support
Slightly reduced AR performance

Option 3 - Progressive Web App:

Works in mobile browsers
No app store approval needed
Limited camera/voice capabilities
Good for MVP testing

AI & Vision System
Computer Vision:
Image Analysis API Options:
Option A - Google Cloud Vision AI:

Object detection and labeling
Landmark recognition
Good for general structure identification
$$$ Cost: ~$1.50 per 1000 images

Option B - OpenAI GPT-4 Vision:

Superior understanding of context
Natural language descriptions
Can reason about engineering principles
$$$ Cost: ~$0.01 per image

Option C - Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet Vision (Recommended):

Excellent technical understanding
Detailed structural analysis
Strong reasoning capabilities
Can handle complex engineering queries
$$$ Cost: Similar to GPT-4

Option D - Custom Model:

Fine-tuned on civil engineering images
Offline capability possible
Higher accuracy for specific elements
Requires training data and expertise
Use TensorFlow Lite or Core ML

Recommended Hybrid Approach:

Use Claude/GPT-4V for initial recognition and analysis
Fine-tuned model for quick element detection
Fallback to general vision API if needed

Voice System
Speech-to-Text (User Input):
Option A - Native Device APIs:

iOS Speech Framework (best for iPhone)
Android Speech Recognition (best for Android)
Free and fast
Good accuracy in quiet environments
Limited in noisy construction sites

Option B - Google Cloud Speech-to-Text:

Superior noise cancellation
Multiple language support
Streaming recognition
$$$ Cost: ~$0.006 per 15 seconds

Option C - OpenAI Whisper:

Open-source option
Excellent accuracy
Can run on-device (large model size)
Free if self-hosted

Text-to-Speech (App Voice):
Option A - Native Device TTS:

iOS AVSpeechSynthesizer
Android TextToSpeech
Free and natural-sounding
Multiple voices and languages

Option B - ElevenLabs / Google Cloud TTS:

More natural, expressive voices
Better for conversational feel
$$$ Cost: ~$0.30 per 1 million characters

Conversational AI:
Option A - OpenAI GPT-4 / Anthropic Claude API:

Powers the intelligent conversation
Maintains context across multiple turns
Generates technical explanations
Integrates with vision analysis
$$$ Cost: ~$0.03 per 1000 tokens

Option B - Voice-Native Model (Future):

OpenAI Realtime API
End-to-end voice without text conversion
Natural interruptions and turn-taking
Currently limited availability

PART 5: EXAMPLE INTERACTIONS
Example 1: Student Learning
Scenario: Civil engineering student at construction site during internship
[Student points camera at exposed column reinforcement]

App: "I can see longitudinal reinforcement bars in what appears to be a column under construction. This looks like a rectangular RCC column with 8 main bars of approximately 16mm diameter. Would you like me to explain the reinforcement design?"

Student: "Yes, why are there ties around the main bars?"

App: "Great question! Those are called lateral ties or stirrups. They serve three important purposes: First, they hold the main longitudinal bars in position during concrete pouring. Second, they prevent the bars from buckling outward under compression loads. Third, they provide shear resistance. For this column size, the ties are likely 8mm diameter bars spaced at 150mm intervals, as per IS 456 requirements. The spacing is kept closer near the top and bottom of the column - around 100mm - because that's where maximum stress occurs. Should I explain the design calculations?"

Student: "What's the concrete grade for this?"

App: "From the construction context and column size, this is likely M25 or M30 grade concrete. M25 means the concrete has a compressive strength of 25 MPa after 28 days of curing. For multi-story buildings, M25 is the minimum grade typically used for columns. You can confirm this by checking the concrete delivery challan or asking the site engineer. Would you like to know how to perform a slump test to check concrete quality?"
Example 2: Quality Inspection
[Site engineer points at freshly cast beam]

App: "I see a freshly cast concrete beam with visible formwork still in place. The beam appears to be around 300mm wide and 600mm deep. How can I help you with this?"

Engineer: "Check if the cover is adequate"

App: "To check concrete cover, I'd need to see the reinforcement cage before casting, or we'd need to use a cover meter. However, based on IS 456:2000, for beams in normal exposure conditions, the minimum cover should be 25mm for main reinforcement and 20mm for stirrups. For moderate or severe exposure, it increases to 30-45mm. Can you show me the reinforcement before the concrete was poured, or would you like me to explain how to use a cover meter?"

Engineer: "The curing is important, what should we do?"

App: "Excellent focus on curing - it's critical for strength development! For this beam, you should: 1) Keep the concrete continuously moist for at least 7 days, preferably 14 days. 2) Start curing within 6-8 hours after casting. 3) Use methods like ponding water on the top surface, covering with wet burlap sacks, or applying curing compounds. 4) Don't let it dry out - concrete gains about 50% strength in the first 7 days. In hot weather, increase curing duration. Should I explain the strength development curve?"
Example 3: Foundation Analysis
[Points at excavated foundation]

App: "I can see an excavated foundation pit with what appears to be preparation for an isolated footing. The excavation looks approximately 2 meters deep. What would you like to know about this foundation?"

User: "What type of foundation is this and why this depth?"

App: "This appears to be an isolated pad footing - the most common type for buildings with column loads. The 2-meter depth is chosen based on several factors: First, the foundation must reach below the depth of seasonal soil moisture changes, which is typically 1.5-2 meters in most Indian soils. Second, it needs to reach a soil layer with adequate bearing capacity. Third, it should be below any roots or organic matter. The actual depth is determined by soil investigation reports. For this size, the soil bearing capacity is likely 150-200 kN/m². Would you like me to explain how engineers calculate the footing size?"

User: "Yes, explain the calculation"

App: "Sure! The footing design follows this process: First, calculate the total load coming from the column - this includes dead load from the building structure, live load from occupancy, and sometimes earthquake loads. Let's say the total load is 1000 kN. Next, check the safe bearing capacity of soil from the geotechnical report - assume 150 kN/m². Then use the formula: Footing area = Total load / Bearing capacity. So, 1000 / 150 = 6.67 square meters. For a square footing, that's about 2.6m x 2.6m. Engineers add 10-15% safety margin, so final size might be 3m x 3m. The depth depends on the structural design for bending and shear. Does this help?"

FINAL RECOMMENDATIONS
Start with MVP Focus:

Implement solid conversational AI
Test with real civil engineering students

Priority 2: Knowledge Depth

Fast response times

Technology Recommendations:
For MVP:

Weeks 3-4: Mobile app UI, camera integration, voice interface
Weeks 5-6: Connect frontend to backend, end-to-end testing

Critical Success Factors:

Simple UX: Must work with gloves on a construction site
Fast Responses: Students won't wait 30 seconds per query
Context Awareness: Remember the conversation flow
Educational Value: Teach, don't just identify


Now build this revolutionary AI tool that transforms how civil engineering is learned and practiced in the field! 🏗️📱🤖

**Envisioning AI App**

I'm now concretizing the idea for CivilVision AI, a mobile app for civil engineers. It's becoming clearer: AI-powered real-time object recognition combined with voice interaction for on-site learning and information access. The application's goal is to revolutionize the way civil engineers learn, communicate, and work.


**Analyzing Structural Elements**

I've been drilling down into the technical architecture. The plan is to use React for a single-page app with Tailwind CSS for styling. For the AI, I'm leaning heavily on the Gemini API. Specifically, Gemini 3 Flash/Pro for image analysis, Gemini Live for the voice interface, and regular Gemini for chat and text explanations. The app will require camera and microphone permissions, and I'm planning to store some basic app information in a `metadata.json` file.


**Mapping App Structure**

I'm now sketching out the detailed file structure.  I've got the `index.html` with Tailwind, React mounting in `index.tsx`, and the core components defined: layout, camera, voice, and analysis.  My plan is to encapsulate Gemini calls within a service file and define clear types. I'm focusing on crafting a system instruction for Gemini to act as a highly knowledgeable civil engineer. This app design will incorporate image analysis, followed by real-time voice interaction.


**Designing UI Components**

I'm now focusing on the UI/UX. The app will be mobile-first with a portrait orientation, large buttons, a camera HUD with a target box and tooltips. There will also be a voice HUD with a waveform and a status indicator. I'm finalizing the file structure, defining the types, and planning the Gemini API interactions. I'm using `gemini-3-flash-preview` for image analysis and text, and `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-09-2025` for live voice interactions. I'll need `camera` and `microphone` permissions, and I'm deciding on state management for analysis objects, live session status, and transcription history.


**Refining App Capabilities**

I'm now iterating on the core functionalities. I've decided to avoid `react-dropzone` and prioritize responsive design using Tailwind. For image analysis, I'll leverage `generateContent` with image parts. I'm focusing on incorporating IS 456, IS 800, and other relevant Indian standards into the system prompt for tailored civil engineering expertise. Real-time voice feedback is planned through the Live API.

If you are unsure, ask the user to show a different angle or provide more context.
`;

payload.text:
Enhance the CivilVision AI app with these additional features:

**1. Universal Civil Engineering Object Recognition:**
Expand beyond structural elements to identify and analyze ANY civil engineering-related object or structure:
- **Furniture & Fixtures**: Benches, tables, stairs, railings - explain materials, load capacity, fabrication methods, anchoring systems
- **Infrastructure**: Roads, pavements, drainage systems, manholes, retaining walls, boundary walls
- **Utilities**: Water tanks, septic systems, electrical conduits, plumbing fixtures
- **Site Elements**: Scaffolding, formwork, construction equipment, temporary structures
- **Landscape Features**: Paving, kerbs, garden walls, ramps, outdoor stairs
- **Building Components**: Doors, windows, partitions, false ceilings, flooring systems

**For Each Object, Provide:**
- **Material identification** (concrete, steel, wood, composite, etc.)
- **Fabrication/construction method** (cast-in-place, precast, welded, bolted, etc.)
- **Load-bearing capacity** (calculate based on dimensions and material)
- **Structural analysis** (stress points, support system, connections)
- **Design standards** (relevant IS codes and specifications)
- **Cost estimation** (materials, labor, approximate budget)
- **Durability & maintenance** (expected lifespan, maintenance needs)

**Example - Concrete Bench Analysis:**
"This is a precast concrete bench, approximately 1.8m long, 0.45m wide, and 0.45m high. Construction: Reinforced concrete with 10mm bars in a mesh pattern. Load capacity: Designed for approximately 400-500 kg distributed load (4-5 people). The bench is anchored to the ground with embedded steel plates. Material: Likely M25 grade concrete with a smooth finish. Typical cost: ₹3,000-5,000 per bench including installation."

**2. Image Upload Instead of Live Camera:**
Replace or supplement real-time camera with:
- **Photo upload from gallery** (analyze existing photos)
- **Multiple image upload** (upload 2-5 images of same structure from different angles for better analysis)
- **Drag-and-drop web interface** (for desktop users)
- **Share from other apps** (WhatsApp, email, cloud storage)

**Benefits:**
- No need to be physically present at site
- Can analyze construction photos shared by others
- Review historical project photos
- Better image quality (can retake if blurry)
- Works with professional photographs and drawings

**3. Defect Detection & Quality Control:**
AI should identify construction flaws, defects, and quality issues:

**Detect These Defects:**
- **Concrete Issues**: Honeycombing, cracks, spalling, segregation, bleeding, cold joints, surface defects
- **Reinforcement Problems**: Inadequate cover, rusting, improper spacing, missing ties/stirrups, poor lap lengths
- **Masonry Defects**: Uneven mortar joints, broken bricks, efflorescence, cracks, bulging walls
- **Alignment Issues**: Plumb problems, level deviations, misaligned elements
- **Formwork Problems**: Bulging, leakage, improper bracing
- **Finishing Defects**: Uneven surfaces, poor plastering, water seepage stains
- **Structural Cracks**: Distinguish between structural vs. non-structural cracks
- **Safety Violations**: Missing safety equipment, unsafe scaffolding, inadequate shoring

**Defect Analysis Should Include:**
- **Severity rating** (Minor / Moderate / Major / Critical)
- **Cause identification** (poor workmanship, material defect, design issue, environmental)
- **Impact assessment** (structural integrity risk, durability concern, aesthetic only)
- **Remedial measures** (how to fix, materials needed, process)
- **Prevention tips** (how to avoid in future)
- **Cost implications** (repair cost estimates)

**Example - Crack Detection:**
"I've detected a diagonal crack approximately 2mm wide running through this beam-column joint. Severity: MAJOR. Cause: This appears to be a structural crack, possibly due to inadequate reinforcement at the joint or overloading. Impact: Could compromise structural integrity if not addressed. Remedy: Consult a structural engineer immediately for load assessment. Likely requires epoxy injection and potentially additional strengthening with carbon fiber wraps or steel plates. Estimated repair cost: ₹15,000-30,000 depending on extent."

**Implementation Summary:**
- Support both camera capture AND image upload
- Recognize any civil engineering object (not just major structures)
- Calculate loads, materials, and costs for everyday items
- Scan images for defects and provide quality control feedback
- Generate detailed inspection reports with severity ratings

Integrate these features into the existing conversational voice app architecture with the same AI-powered analysis and explanation capabilities.

---

**What This Adds:**
✅ Universal object recognition (benches, railings, anything civil-related)
✅ Image upload functionality (analyze photos from gallery)
✅ Load calculations for everyday structures
✅ Defect detection and quality control
✅ Remedial recommendations for construction flaws
✅ Severity ratings and repair cost estimates

**Extending Recognition Scope**

I'm currently focused on expanding the object recognition capabilities of `CivilVision AI`. The goal is to move beyond the current limited set of recognizable objects and encompass a much broader range of civil engineering elements. This involves considering furniture, infrastructure, and even utilities for identification.


**Developing Analysis Capabilities**

I've just added image upload functionality to `CivilVision AI`, allowing users to analyze images directly from their devices. My focus now is on integrating defect detection and quality control.  I'm updating the `analyzeImage` function to recognize flaws like honeycombing and cracks, along with their severity. The goal is to provide specific remedial measures and even a cost estimate for repairs. UI updates are in progress to present this new data clearly.


**Adding Deep Analysis Features**

I'm currently working on updating the `types.ts` file to add `defects`, `severity`, `loadCapacity`, `costEstimate`, and `remedialMeasures` to `StructuralAnalysis`. I'm also revising the system prompt in `constants.ts` to reflect the expanded scope, including "Universal Recognition" and "Defect Expert" capabilities.  The new "Upload from Gallery" feature in `CameraInterface.tsx` is implemented, and the `AnalysisView.tsx` will display a new "Quality & Defects" section.


**Adapting New Schemas**

I'm now integrating the new data schema into the `services/gemini.ts` file.  I've already updated `CameraInterface.tsx` to handle image uploads. I'm also preparing `AnalysisView.tsx` to display the enhanced analysis, with a focus on a visually appealing presentation of the new data points.

## **TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION NOTES**

### **For Knowledge Section:**

**Database Schema:**
```sql
categories (id, name, icon, order, description)
subcategories (id, category_id, name, order)
topics (id, subcategory_id, title, slug, content, formulas, diagrams, examples, related_topics, created_at, updated_at)
user_progress (user_id, topic_id, completed, bookmarked, notes, last_viewed)
```

**Content Storage:**
- **Main content**: Markdown with LaTeX (store in PostgreSQL or MongoDB)
- **Formulas**: Render with KaTeX/MathJax on frontend
- **Diagrams**: SVG files stored in CDN (AWS S3, Cloudflare)
- **Videos**: Host on YouTube, embed links
- **Calculators**: React components with calculation logic

**Search Implementation:**
- Full-text search (PostgreSQL tsvector or Elasticsearch)
- Formula search (parse LaTeX, index symbols)
- Fuzzy matching for typos
- Relevance ranking by topic importance and user history

### **For Settings Section:**

**User Preferences Schema:**
```json
{
  "user_id": "12345",
```

**Settings Storage:**
- Store in user document/record
- Sync to cloud on change (debounced)
- Cache locally for instant access
- Version settings schema for migrations

**Personal Branding Section:**
- **Static content** (your bio, links) hardcoded in app
- **Dynamic content** (portfolio projects) fetched from API
- **LinkedIn data**: Use LinkedIn API or scrape your public profile (ethically)
- **Portfolio integration**: If your portfolio has an API, fetch latest projects/posts
- **Fallback**: If APIs unavailable, display static content

**Defining the Website's Purpose**

I'm starting to crystallize the essence of CivilVision AI. It's built for civil engineers and students. The core will involve real-time structural analysis and design tools. I'm focusing on concisely explaining this, built upon the code and existing context. My aim is to make it a go-to resource.

**CivilVision AI** is a professional-grade, mobile-first intelligence platform designed specifically for civil engineering students and field professionals. It acts as an "AI pair-engineer" that bridges the gap between physical site conditions and technical engineering standards.

### Core Capabilities:
*   **Structural Vision:** Uses the Gemini 3 Pro engine to identify structural elements (RCC columns, beams, foundation types, metro tunnels) in real-time via your camera or uploaded site photos.
*   **Intelligent Inspection:** Automatically detects structural defects like **honeycombing, spalling, and corrosion**, providing severity ratings and repair protocols.
*   **Expert Consulting:** Features a specialized chatbot and voice-enabled assistant trained on global engineering standards and **Indian Standard (IS) codes** (e.g., IS 456, IS 800).
*   **Executive Summaries:** Translates complex structural data into simplified "Plain English" briefs for quick site updates and non-technical stakeholders.
*   **Engineering Knowledge Base:** Includes a deep database covering 24 core domains, from Soil Mechanics and Statics to advanced Bridge and TBM Tunneling engineering.

### Visual Identity:
The app features a **"Midnight Blueprint"** aesthetic—utilizing a high-contrast dark theme with technical grid overlays, scanning animations, and a precise, mono-spaced typography system that mimics engineering drafting software.

```
σ = P / A
```

"""
CivilVision AI: Model Fine-Tuning Utility
This script extracts corrected site images and labels from the Training_Queue 
to perform transfer learning on the Vision model.
"""

import json
import os
import requests
from PIL import Image
import io
import base64

# Configuration
TRAINING_QUEUE_FILE = "training_queue.json"
MODEL_ENDPOINT = "https://civilvision-api.engine/retrain"
MIN_BATCH_SIZE = 10

def retrain_from_overrides():
    if not os.path.exists(TRAINING_QUEUE_FILE):
        print("[!] No retraining queue found.")
        return

    with open(TRAINING_QUEUE_FILE, "r") as f:
        queue = json.load(f)

    if len(queue) < MIN_BATCH_SIZE:
        print(f"[*] Batch size {len(queue)} too small. Waiting for {MIN_BATCH_SIZE} corrections.")
        return

    print(f"[*] Initializing retraining for {len(queue)} site corrections...")

    processed_data = []
    for entry in queue:
        # 1. Logic: Load image from hash/base64
        # 2. Logic: Extract verified labels (e.g. M20 instead of M25)
        # 3. Logic: Prepare tensor for backpropagation
        processed_data.append({
            "image_hash": entry["hash"],
            "ground_truth": entry["labels"],
            "timestamp": entry["timestamp"]
        })

    # Triggering Neural Weights Update
    try:
        response = requests.post(MODEL_ENDPOINT, json=processed_data)
        if response.status_code == 200:
            print("[✓] Model weights updated successfully. Local accuracy optimized.")
            # Clear queue after success
            os.remove(TRAINING_QUEUE_FILE)
        else:
            print("[x] Retraining failed at endpoint.")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[x] Connection Error: {e}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    retrain_from_overrides()
